item.title: Abeno Harukas: Japan's Tallest Skyscraper View — Guide
item.description: Abeno Harukas, rising 300 metres above Tennoji, was Japan’s tallest building on its completion in 2014 and remains among the very tallest. It is a vertical city — a department store, a hotel, an art museum and offices stacked in one tower — but for visitors the draw is Harukas 300, the observation complex on the top three floors. Floor-to-ceiling glass wraps a full circuit 300 metres up, with an open-air atrium at its heart, giving a genuinely commanding view over Osaka, out to Kobe, Awaji and, on clear days, the mountains beyond.

item.title: Tennoji Park & Keitakuen Garden: Green Heart of the South — Guide
item.description: Tennoji Park spreads beneath the towers of Abeno Harukas, a large and varied green space at the junction of the Tennoji and Shinsekai districts. Its jewel is Keitakuen, a circular strolling garden designed in the early twentieth century around a central pond, once the private garden of the Sumitomo family and a masterpiece of the period. The park also holds Osaka’s zoo, the city art museum and, at its northern edge, a modern lawn plaza lined with cafes and lit in the evening — making it a place equally suited to garden lovers, families and anyone wanting to sit down between sights.

item.title: Spa World Osaka Guide: The Giant Themed Bath Complex
item.description: Beside the retro neon of Shinsekai looms Spa World — a vast, slightly surreal multi-floor bathing complex where you can soak in a Roman bath, a Finnish sauna, an Islamic-tiled pool, a Balinese spa, and a Japanese rotenburo, all under one roof. Part onsen, part water park, part kitsch theme attraction, it’s one of Osaka’s most fun and affordable ways to relax — a place to spend hours bathing, sweating, swimming, and recovering from a day of takoyaki and walking.
